selection_input: non-O1 validation corpus results ONLY; no O1 outcome may influence selection
eligibility_requirements_all_must_pass: every structural equivalence gate passes (row IDs, task hashes, prompt tokens, action mapping, axis/sign/alpha mapping, stream and seed mapping, record schema, canonical ordering)
parser/verifier recomputation passes on every record
action and seed mapping are exact
intervention semantics pass (per-row position, per-row delta, no padding writes, no repeated decode-time injection, realized delta measured)
transport semantics pass (per-row capture, no cross-row mixing, zero-alpha bitwise convention)
resume tests pass (interrupt + resume completes with no missing/duplicate rows)
no missing rows and no duplicate rows in the finalized merge
no OOM during the configuration's benchmark
no unvalidated optimization active (compaction, torch.compile, CUDA graphs, alternate attention all OFF unless separately equivalence-passed)

throughput stable (spread <= 25% of decode tokens/s across four equal wall-clock windows of each execution stream's steady state within one execute_rows pass; the worst stream is the configuration's spread)
scientific configuration unchanged (axes, K=8, CRN, Latin square, alpha grid, parser, verifier, transport, task populations, seed policy)
selection_rule: among eligible configurations select highest verified completed rows/hour on the non-O1 validation corpus benchmark
tie_break_order: 2: lower semantic complexity: REFERENCE_SERIAL, then B200_REPLICA, then B200_BATCHED without compaction, then B200_BATCHED with compaction
3: smaller worker/batch count (workers+batch sum, then workers)
fallback: B200_REPLICA is the designated fallback if no B200_BATCHED configuration passes the equivalence gates; REFERENCE_SERIAL is always eligible as the terminal fallback PROVIDED every scientific and safety gate passes for it (structural, parser/verifier, mapping, intervention, transport, resume, rows, no OOM, free HBM, no unvalidated optimization, configuration unchanged); only the throughput-stability performance gate is waived for the terminal fallback, and the waiver is recorded in BACKEND_SELECTION.json
prohibitions: no selection based on any O1 task outcome
no post-hoc re-benchmarking to flip a selection
an ineligible configuration can never be selected regardless of throughput

amendments.why: the v1 measurement executed the corpus in four CONTIGUOUS row quartiles and compared rows/s, which measures corpus ordering: on the local synthetic benchmark every backend showed the same slow third quartile (rows 192-287 generate more tokens) and 7 of 10 configurations, the reference included, failed the gate. On the accelerator that is an abort at BACKEND_SELECT after the benchmark has been paid for. The threshold (25%) is unchanged; the quantity is now the accelerator's decode rate over time, per execution stream, so a replica worker's model-load ramp and uneven finish are not read as instability either.
amendments.scientific_impact: none: selection input only; the sealed O1 package, the equivalence gates and the corpus are untouched
